cells.tense: Right now the arrangements you keep are holding, and they carry more than you notice.
cells.act: notice what you already know before you reason about it
cells.ask: When several parts of a shared thing pull at you at once, catch what you know about it before you build the case, then start there.
cells.core:
In what gets carried between people, you can set out a shape others can follow without being told. A gathering, a practice, the way something gets passed down — under your hand it comes out clear, and people move through it without stumbling. That reliability is quiet, and it is not small.

The part to feed is your own knowing. Before you reason about what should come next here, something in you has already settled which piece matters; it lands before any argument for it arrives. Let that be where you start instead of assembling the case first. You'll still assemble it. You'll just be assembling it behind something you'd already settled. What that costs is being thorough before you move, and being thorough first is what you've been paying with.

cells.tense: You are building the next version of this shared thing before anyone has asked for it.
cells.act: name the mechanism in one line and change nothing
cells.ask: For what moves between people, put in one line what keeps driving you to organize it further — and change nothing you named.
cells.core:
Something gets taken up, and before it has sat with anyone it has a form, a sequence, a proper way. The shape does the job it was built for; it has also begun doing the standing-in for the thing itself. You are already working on the next version of it, and nobody has asked.

Take this arrangement and look at it from far enough back to see what it is for, apart from any single time it happens. Then put in a line what keeps moving you to add more to it. No plan, no repair. Seeing that plainly is the whole of this, and it doesn't need the next draft. Holding it open will be uncomfortable, and that discomfort is what the view costs.
cells.sheetLine: You give it a shape before it has had a chance to live.
cells.verb: organizing what's loose into a shape others can follow
cells.place: where meaning is carried between people

cells.tense: The pieces have been sitting in front of you for a while now, and they have not come together.
cells.act: let one structure collapse that could not hold
cells.ask: Pick one shared arrangement here that has been quietly failing, stop propping it up this week, and stand back while it goes.
cells.core:
In the place where meaning moves between people, nothing is assembling. There are pieces you know belong together and no order that puts them there, so what you owe stays vague, and the vagueness has been read by others as not caring. That reading is wrong. The ordering impulse is not gone from you; it is going unfed.

Stop holding up one thing that was not going to hold. Not everything — one. An arrangement you've been keeping alive by upkeep alone, that's visibly not working and nobody has stopped. Let it come down and stay in the gap without rushing to fill it. The clear ground is the point. Rebuilding comes later, and it comes easier on a floor that isn't already crowded.

cells.tense: You are arranging things here right now, and if asked, you would say you were not.
cells.act: let the thing end that is already over
cells.ask: Something shared you still keep going for other people is finished — stop carrying it this week and leave the space it took.
cells.core:
The structure that holds a shared thing together is often yours, and the account you give of it is that it runs itself. People come to you and find the shape already set — the way something is done here, the order it goes in — and you'd say that's just how it is. Meanwhile you have been the one setting it.

Something you have kept going is already finished, and upkeep is the only thing left of it. End it, on your side. That may be a sentence to someone or a note to no one. What follows is a lighter grip and a plainer name for what you have been doing. Endings are trusted here; the next form arrives once the old one has stopped.
cells.sheetLine: The order people rely on is yours, and you would call it no one's.
